Reproducible Research v0.1.2 — complete trajectory-to-report

Source: vignettes/articles/reproducible-research-release.Rmd
reproducible-research-release.Rmd

Reproduce the Scientific Core 2.0 software release

Official release: AquaTrajectories v0.1.2, published 21 November 2026. This is an engineering-qualified reproducibility release, not a claim of independently measured fish biology.

Public R API179 documented exported functions
Executed R code coverage89.33% measured; release gate at 80%
Cross-platform qualification24 workloads per OS · Linux, Windows, macOS

Five milestones completed

Scientific Core 2.0 workstream Implementation and evidence
01 — Architecture and scientific API Unit-aware 2D/3D analysis without obligatory video, PRs #100–102
02 — General trajectory QC2 Original-row eligibility, exclusions, missing data and sensitivity, PR #103
03 — Numerical Validation 2.0 Independent numerical oracles, metamorphic properties and failure fixtures, PR #104
04 — Publication Visualization 2.0 Gap-aware plots, provenance and SVG/PDF/PNG/TIFF journal output, PR #105
05 — Reproducible Research Release Measured source coverage and memory/runtime, exact three-OS gates and frozen example, PR #106

These software qualifications do not require the user to run a detector or collect video. They do not validate every possible statistical estimator/input combination or any welfare claim.

The independent, locked numerical example

The released synthetic fixture contains 17 rows across three invented fish, with a deliberately missing observation, a frame discontinuity and an excessive displacement. The unchanged original data file has SHA-256:

b940aedc80b9ca0a2355b5fcc1912cc233ecf6318044bed4d7449ca7ee0be2bc

Synthetic track Raw observations Eligible adjacent steps Accepted distance
0001 5 3 3 cm
0002 6 3 3 cm
0003 6 4 4 cm
Total 17 10 10 cm

Check the original source at the immutable tag and rerun the entire chain:

git clone --branch v0.1.2 --depth 1 https://github.com/stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories.git
cd AquaTrajectories
R CMD INSTALL .
Rscript scripts/release05_example.R release05-example
python scripts/release05_verify.py --out release05-example

The R workflow exports an original-row QC ledger, four publication figure types in SVG, PDF, PNG and TIFF, an interpretable Markdown report, input/output hashes and figure-to-input provenance. The independent Python standard-library implementation re-derives the 10 eligible movements and length from the source CSV and checks the exported evidence. It refuses altered source rows, numeric reports and figures. This is a controlled synthetic demonstration, not new fish measurements.

Measured performance, with explicit units and limits

The release qualification recorded 89.33% instrumented R test coverage using covr, above its 80% gate; coverage is not a percentage of scientific accuracy. The full benchmark exercised 24 measured workloads per OS on Linux, Windows and macOS (2D/3D, three dataset sizes, four operations). Median seconds for selected 20,000-observation benchmarks:

Workload Linux Windows macOS
2D path summary 0.0458 0.0388 0.0321
2D school geometry 3.2856 2.2616 2.0713
2D QC2 lineage 0.2287 0.1375 0.1506
3D school geometry 3.3782 2.3079 1.9424

These observed times were measured on different GitHub runners; they are not controlled speed comparisons across operating systems. The allocation-memory metric is R allocated memory, not peak resident memory. View all benchmark tables and exact measurement definitions.

Citation/version rule: cite v0.1.2 CITATION.cff and the versioned tag. Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24262905 belongs specifically to historical v0.1.1; no v0.1.2 Zenodo DOI or CRAN availability is asserted.

Scientific limits: independent fish detector/identity accuracy, calibrated underwater XYZ, empirical uncertainty coverage, stress or welfare diagnosis, real animal–computer-interaction safety and causal effects require separate external evidence. Synthetic software gates cannot certify those findings.
